transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
Well, it’s mainly when I get into a slow elevator or some small room that’s locked. Right away my chest kind of jumps, and I feel like I need to get back out before I can even think straight.
Do you ever experience sudden feelings of intense fear or panic when you're in those situations, like elevators or locked rooms?

Yes. As soon as I step into a slow elevator, or if I’m in a small room that’s locked, it hits me right away. My chest kind of jumps, and I get this strong feeling like I need to get out before I can even think straight.
Do these panic feelings happen only in those specific situations like elevators or locked rooms, or do they sometimes come on suddenly even when you’re not in those places?
It’s really only when I’m in those places, like a slow elevator or a small locked room. That’s when it hits right away—my chest jumps and I just feel like I have to get back out.
Do you find yourself actively avoiding elevators or small locked rooms because of these feelings, even when you don’t have to be in them right away?

Yes, I do. These days I’ll take the stairs if I can, and I’ve passed on archive jobs at the museum because I didn’t want to be back in those closed-in spaces. If I really can’t avoid it, I’ll ask a friend to wait nearby. I feel a bit foolish doing that, but it helps me get through it.
Have you ever had a panic attack in a situation that wasn't related to being in a slow elevator or a locked room?
No, I don’t think so. I can’t remember having that kind of panic out of nowhere. It’s pretty much tied to those elevator or locked-room situations.
Do you feel like your reaction in those situations is more intense or extreme than what most people would experience in the same circumstances?

Yes, I think it is more than most folks would feel. I know a little storage room or an elevator at the museum isn’t really the same as being locked up, but once I see there’s no window and that door shuts tight, my mind treats it like trouble right away.

Do you feel that your panic in elevators or locked rooms is in proportion to the actual risk or danger present in those situations, or do you feel like your reaction is stronger than the situation really calls for?

It’s stronger than the situation really calls for. I know a small storage room or an elevator at the museum isn’t the same as actually being locked up somewhere dangerous, but as soon as I see there’s no window and the door shuts tight, my mind just treats it like trouble.
Has this fear of elevators and locked rooms caused you significant distress or affected your daily life, such as limiting your work opportunities or social activities?

Yes, it has some. I’ve had to turn down a few museum docent tasks, and I’ve skipped some gallery events because I didn’t want to end up dealing with elevators or those closed-in rooms. It hasn’t stopped my whole life, but it’s made my volunteering and outings more limited than they used to be.
Have you ever felt afraid or anxious in situations where you weren’t in a slow elevator or locked room, like being outside alone, in a crowd, or on public transportation?
No, not really. I don’t think I get that same fear just being outside, or in a crowd, or riding somewhere. It’s mostly when I feel shut in, like with the elevator or a locked room.
Do you start feeling anxious or panicky even when you're just thinking about going into an elevator or a locked room, before you actually get there?

Yes, I do some, even before I’m there. If I know I’m going to have to use a slow elevator or go into a small locked room, I start getting worked up thinking about it. And once I actually step in, my chest jumps right away and I just feel like I need to get back out before I can think straight.
Do you ever experience similar panic attacks in other situations that are not elevators or locked rooms, such as when you're in open spaces, high places, or around animals?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed that kind of panic in open places or around animals or anything like that. It’s really more when I feel closed in.
Are there any other specific situations, besides elevators and locked rooms, where you feel similar panic or anxiety even if you're not currently in those situations?

Yeah, sometimes a little storage room can do it too. Like if there’s no window and the door shuts tight, my mind treats it like trouble right away, even though I know it’s not the same as being locked up. An elevator at a museum or someplace like that can set me off the same way.
